about.role: Developer and founder of Bracket Studio
body: I build websites, internal tools and apps for businesses with a concrete problem to solve — not showcase projects.

When you write to Bracket Studio, the person who answers is the person who actually builds your product: no salesperson in between, no questions passed on to someone else. From the first call to launch, you always know who you're talking to.

items.question: Who actually does the work?
items.answer: The person building your product is the person you talk to. No salesperson who sells you something and then disappears, no questions passed on to someone else: you ask, and the person with their hands on it answers.

items.question: Do I need to understand the technology?
items.answer: No. Our job is to ask you the right questions and turn the answers into something that works. If we explain something and it isn't clear, that's on us, not you.

items.question: Will I be locked in to you?
items.answer: No. The code, the domain and the servers are 100% in your name, from day one. If you ever want to move on, you take everything with you and anyone can carry on the work.

items.question: And afterwards? If something breaks?
items.answer: We stay on it. Monitoring, maintenance and changes: whoever built it keeps looking after it once it's live.

items.question: How do we start?
items.answer: With a free call, no commitment. You tell us what you need, we tell you whether we can help and what it costs. If it isn't a fit, we say so.

cta.title: Got another question?
cta.text: Call or write: half an hour is usually enough to work out whether it makes sense to work together.

good.title: Your site is in good shape.
good.body: We found no serious problems. Below are the few things that could still be polished, in order of importance.

average.title: It works, but it's losing people along the way.
average.body: Your site does its job, but a few things are costing you visits and enquiries. They're few and concrete — here they are, without the jargon.

poor.title: Your site is losing customers along the way.
poor.body: People opening it on a phone wait too long, or don't find what they came for. The fixes are few and concrete: here they are, ordered by what they're costing you.

dataSource.field: Measured from real visitors to your site over the last 28 days.
dataSource.lab: Measured just now, simulating a mid-range phone on a 4G connection.

result.screenshotAlt: How {host} looks on a phone screen
result.screenshotCaption: Your site, as a phone sees it
result.metricsSubtitle: Three numbers no visitor ever reads — and all three of which they feel.
result.categoriesSubtitle: From 0 to 100, using Google's own thresholds: above 90 is good, below 50 needs work.
result.findingsSubtitle: Ordered by what it's costing you. We stop at the five things that genuinely matter: underneath there are dozens of technical details you don't need.
result.noFindings: We found none of the problems we check for. That's rare — whoever built this did good work.
result.footnote: Based on Google PageSpeed Insights, the same tool Google uses to assess websites. It's a snapshot of your home page taken right now: a good starting point, not a full audit of the whole site.

loadTime.label: How long before anything appears
loadTime.good: Excellent: visitors see your content straight away, with no time to get impatient.
loadTime.average: A little slow. On a phone connection away from home, this is the moment people hit back.
loadTime.poor: Too slow. A good share of the people arriving from Google leave before they see anything at all.

stability.label: How much the page jumps while loading
stability.good: Steady: nothing shifts under your finger while the page finishes loading.
stability.average: Things move around while it loads. That's why people occasionally tap the wrong button.
stability.poor: The page rearranges itself a lot while loading: anyone tapping early often ends up somewhere they didn't mean to.

responsiveness.label: How long it ignores your taps
responsiveness.good: Responsive: tap something and it reacts immediately.
responsiveness.average: It sometimes doesn't react to taps right away. People describe this as a site that “freezes”.
responsiveness.poor: For a long stretch the site doesn't respond to taps at all: it feels broken even when it isn't.

speed.label: Speed
speed.what: How long a customer waits before they can actually use the site on a phone.

google.label: Google visibility
google.what: Whether the site gives Google what it needs to understand you and show you in results.

everyone.label: Usable by everyone
everyone.what: Whether it still works for people with poor eyesight, unsteady hands, or a phone in bright sun.

care.label: Technical care
care.what: Security, hidden errors, and whether things were done properly under the hood.

https.title: The site isn't secure
https.impact: Browsers show “Not secure” next to your address, and Google ranks sites without the padlock lower. It's the first thing to fix, and it usually takes hours.

viewport.title: It isn't built for phones
viewport.impact: People opening it on a phone get the desktop version shrunk down and have to pinch-zoom to read. Most leave without trying.

blockedFromGoogle.title: You're telling Google not to show you
blockedFromGoogle.impact: There's an instruction in the site asking search engines to ignore it. While it's there you will never appear on Google, whatever else you do.

httpStatus.title: The site responds with an error
httpStatus.impact: The server doesn't return the page the way it should. Google reads that as a broken site and stops offering it in results.

title.title: The title Google shows is missing
title.impact: It's the clickable line in search results. Without one, Google invents it from your content — usually badly.

description.title: The description under your Google result is missing
description.impact: Those two lines are what convince someone to click you instead of the competitor above or below you. Writing them takes ten minutes.

linkText.title: Some links just say “click here”
linkText.impact: Neither people nor Google can tell where they lead. Saying what's on the other side helps both, and earns you positions.

crawlableLinks.title: Google can't follow some of your links
crawlableLinks.impact: They're built in a way search engines don't read: the pages behind them risk never appearing in results at all.

slowServer.title: Your server takes too long to answer
slowServer.impact: Before showing anything, the site spends a long time simply waiting. It's often the hosting: changing it is the quickest way to win back seconds.

heavyPage.title: The page is too heavy
heavyPage.impact: Anyone opening it on mobile data downloads a large file before seeing anything — and on a slow connection the wait doubles.

heavyImages.title: Your images weigh more than they need to
heavyImages.impact: This is almost always the number one cause of slowness. The very same photos, saved in the right format, can weigh a fifth with no visible loss of quality.

blockingResources.title: The site waits for non-urgent things before showing itself
blockingResources.impact: Some parts block your content from appearing even though they aren't needed straight away. Moving them is a quick job you feel on the first load.

unusedCode.title: The site loads code it never uses
unusedCode.impact: This almost always comes from themes and plugins: visitors download features their page doesn't need, and wait for nothing.

invisibleText.title: Text stays invisible while loading
invisibleText.impact: For a moment the page looks empty, then the words appear. Anyone arriving at that moment assumes the site is broken.

contrast.title: Some text is hard to read
contrast.impact: Text and background are too close in colour: on a phone screen in daylight they become unreadable. You lose everyone unwilling to squint.

smallTargets.title: Some buttons are too small to tap
smallTargets.impact: On a phone, people miss. If it happens on your “book” or “call” button, that's exactly where you lost the customer.

imageAlt.title: Your images have no description
imageAlt.impact: Google can't see photos: it reads the description attached to them. Without one you lose Google Images traffic, and anyone using a screen reader has no idea what they're looking at.

formLabels.title: Some form fields have no label
formLabels.impact: People aren't always sure what to type, and anyone using a screen reader simply can't. Forms are where your enquiries come from: they're worth getting right.

namelessControls.title: Some buttons and links have no name
namelessControls.impact: To a blind visitor's phone they're just “button, button, button”. Google also struggles to work out how your site is put together.

language.title: The site's language isn't declared
language.impact: Browsers need it to offer translation, and screen readers to pronounce words correctly. It is quite literally one line of code.

headingOrder.title: Your headings are out of order
headingOrder.impact: Google uses headings to understand what you're about and what matters most. Used as plain bold text, you throw that advantage away.

consoleErrors.title: The site throws errors while being used
consoleErrors.impact: You can't see them, but they mean something isn't working as it should — often the forms or the buttons themselves.

stretchedImages.title: Some images come out distorted
stretchedImages.impact: Photos squashed or stretched out of their real proportions. It's the thing that makes a site look homemade even when everything else is polished.

outdatedCode.title: The site uses parts that are now obsolete
outdatedCode.impact: They still work, but browsers are removing them. Sooner or later something will stop working, and it'll happen without warning.

redirects.title: The site bounces between addresses before it opens
redirects.impact: Every bounce adds waiting before anything appears, and on a phone connection you feel it. It usually goes away by pointing links straight at the right address.

unsizedImages.title: Your images don't declare how big they are
unsizedImages.impact: The browser doesn't know how much room to leave them, so the page rearranges itself while loading. That's why people occasionally tap the wrong button.

canonical.title: The page's official address is declared incorrectly
canonical.impact: It tells Google which address is the real one when the same page can be reached several ways. Get it wrong and Google may index the wrong version — or none at all.

robotsTxt.title: The file that guides Google has errors in it
robotsTxt.impact: It's the instruction sheet search engines read first. Bad lines in it risk them ignoring pages you actually want found.

wins.https: The site is secure: visitors see the padlock next to your address.
wins.mobile: It's built for phones: readable without pinch-zooming.
wins.title: The title Google shows in results is there and in good shape.
wins.description: The description that appears under your Google result is in place.
wins.imageAlt: Your images have descriptions: Google understands them and can show them.
wins.contrast: Text reads clearly, even on a phone in bright sun.
wins.fastServer: Your server answers quickly: the foundations are solid.
wins.crawlable: Google can read the site and put it in its results.
wins.targets: Buttons are big enough to tap accurately with a finger.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains how Bracket Studio collects and uses the personal data of people who visit this site or submit the contact form, under Regulation (EU) 2016/679 ("GDPR").

sections.heading: Data controller
sections.body: Bracket Studio, reachable at info@bracketstudio.it, is the controller for the data collected through this site.

sections.heading: Data collected through the contact form
sections.body: When you submit the contact form we collect your name, email address, project type (optional) and the content of your message. This data is used solely to respond to your request and evaluate a possible collaboration, and is kept for as long as needed to handle the request and any resulting engagement.

sections.heading: Legal basis
sections.body: Processing is based on your consent, given by submitting the form, and on pre-contractual steps requested by you ahead of a possible collaboration.

sections.heading: Data recipients
sections.body: Messages sent through the contact form are delivered to our inbox via Brevo (Sendinblue SA), acting as data processor for email delivery. We do not sell or share your data with third parties for marketing purposes.

sections.heading: Data collected automatically
sections.body: This site does not use profiling cookies or third-party analytics. The only information stored in your browser is your chosen language and theme (light/dark), to remember your preferences — see our cookie policy for details.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You can request access, correction, deletion or restriction of your data at any time by writing to info@bracketstudio.it. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority.

cookiePolicy.title: Cookie policy
cookiePolicy.intro: This site uses a minimal number of cookies and similar technologies, all strictly necessary for the site to work. There are no profiling or third-party advertising cookies.

cookiePolicy.outro: Since these cookies are strictly necessary for the site to function, no prior consent is required. You can still clear them at any time from your browser settings.
